newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian sugar rocked by legal claim against QSC.
newsitem.headline: Australian sugar rocked by legal claim against QSC.

text.p: Aggressive independent sugar refining group Mackay Refined Sugars Pty Ltd has rocked the Australian sugar industry with a A$200 million damages claim against Queensland Sugar Corp (QSC).
The claim, which follows long-running court action by Mackay against Australia's leading refiner CSR Ltd after a failed 1993 merger attempt, came unexpectedly for QSC on Wednesday.
"QSC will vigorously defend legal action expected to be initiated by Mackay Refined Sugars this week," QSC said in a statement.

Allegations by Mackay that QSC in 1994 breached contracts or warranties with Mackay or had acted contrary to the Trade Practices Act were totally without basis, QSC's chief executive David Rutledge said in the statement.
"QSC acted appropriately and in accordance with the law and the interests of the Queensland sugar industry at all times in its dealings with both domestic and export customers," he said.
Executives of Mackay were in meetings and not immediately available for comment on Thursday.
Rutledge told Reuters the action had the potential to destabilise Australia's sugar industry.

"The size of this claim, (as) we understand it ...up to A$200 million, is a very significant sum and I think it has the potential to create uncertainty in the industry and has the potential to that extent to be destabilising," he said.
Mackay's action had not yet been filed as far as QSC knew and formal details had not yet been seen, Rutledge said.
But previous allegations by Mackay were that QSC had given undertakings for even-handed treatment compared with other domestic customers, he said.

These were said to have been given before Mackay entered into a joint-venture with international commodities group ED&F Man to build a sugar refinery in Mackay, on the coast of the state of Queensland, he said. The refinery has been in operation now for three years.
Mackay had alleged that QSC had not complied, had given preferential treatment to other customers and had damaged Mackay as a result, he said.

"We believe that the claim is not well founded and we are happy to go to court if that's where they want to take it. We want that to be done expeditiously to minimise the level of uncertainty to the industry and we believe that we will be vindicated," Rutledge told Reuters.
The Federal Court claim is expected to be lodged Thursday.

"QSC negotiates all contracts individually with customers and consequently there are always variations between contracts. However, all contracts are negotiated ethically and lawfully," Rutledge said in the statement.
The A$200 million action relates to costs and losses alleged to have been incurred by the Mackay Refined Sugars joint-venture, the QSC statement said.
QSC is a statutory body which holds monopoly export rights over the state's annual raw sugar production, whose annual earnings from raw sugar sales totals about A$2 billion.

Mackay launched legal action in New Zealand last October against CSR Ltd subsidiary New Zealand Sugar Corp, seeking about NZ$10 million damages. Mackay alleged the CSR unit intended to eliminate Mackay as a competitor by use of price-cutting power.

The Australian refined sugar market also has been subject to a debilitating price-cutting war for years, primarily between Mackay and CSR. This followed rejection by the then Trade Practices Commission in December 1993 of a proposed merger between operations of CSR, Mackay and international commodities group ED&F Man. Mackay Refined Sugars is a joint-venture between ED&F Man and Mackay Sugar Co-operative.
-- Sydney Newsroom 612-2 9373-1800
